mechanism: Observation-layer replay of exec-WM v1: reclassify every retained move-action transition through the SHIPPED detect_translation/mine code (not a reimplementation) to locate where transition evidence is lost between the frame feed and the rule set.
summary: The 'data starvation' re-diagnosis of exec-WM v1 is REFUTED by its own retained artifact. Across 2394 move-action transitions in 25 games, 51.9% (1243) are already clean single-sprite translations; the feed is rich. In the zero-candidate games the board changes on 85-100% of move actions (lf52 and tr87 at 100% mined ZERO rules; g50t at 74.2% mined four) and median changed-cells is indistinguishable between failing (46) and working (54) games. The loss is entirely inside the extractor, in two over-strict gates: GATE B (detect_translation requires a move to explain EVERY interior diff cell) discards 641 transitions (26.8%) as 'unexplained' whenever any change co-occurs; GATE A (mine() admits a rule only if len(deltas)==1) discards a rule outright on a single dissenting delta, e.g. one blocked move, and also fences blocker mining.
lesson: THREE successive diagnoses of the SAME number were wrong, each corrected only by reading the artifact instead of the prior summary: (1) 'raise the probe budget' - closed arithmetically by the probe histogram; (2) 'BREAK clustering' - refuted, the latch fired zero times and the cause was a mislabelled reason string; (3) 'the observation layer is data-starved' - refuted here, over half the transitions are clean. A fallback-reason string names the gate that FIRED, never the quantity that was MISSING; counting reasons will keep producing new wrong diagnoses. Replay the raw evidence through the shipped classifier instead. Corollary that generalises: when relaxing an upstream filter, check whether an INDEPENDENT downstream gate already prices the risk - here mining is held to a stricter standard (exact consensus) than the arm holds an LLM's guess, which enters as a mere candidate for a 0.90-precision prequential verifier.

prereg.prestated_v2_constraint: a v2 may NOT be a probe-budget tweak; it must widen the rule class / object model (click-addressable objects, non-constant deltas, multi-object dynamics)

design: CPU-only replay, no network, no GPU, no kernel push, zero submission slots. Artifacts re-pulled 2026-08-27 and verified complete (both large logs present; only 0-byte file a legitimately empty __init__.py).
sealed_reading_rule: Diagnostic, not a scored arm: no lc verdict, no board draw, no kill-budget charge. The claim under test was the 08-27 handoff's premise that transition extraction returns EMPTY.
robustness: The reason-tracer is asserted line-by-line against the shipped detect_translation (a drift raises). Union gate is reported instead of majority-replacement precisely because majority ALONE drops a unanimous low-n rule (re86 4->3); the union loses nothing.
why_informative: This null is informative because it CLOSES the last cheap explanation for exec-WM's 31/32 fallback rate and redirects a re-seed that was about to be spent on the wrong layer. The arm was one build away from 'repair the feed' work on a feed that is demonstrably fine. It also re-validates the ORIGINAL sealed bench_meta lesson (the binding constraint is object identification and rule-class coverage, upstream of planner and verifier), which two days of re-diagnosis had drifted away from, and it converts the sealed prestated_v2_constraint from a prohibition into a ranked, measured build order: Gate B (641 transitions) >> Gate A (+12 rules, 2 games made plannable), with Gate A far cheaper.
not_done: No v2 built, no kernel pushed (slot decision; lane_locks.json entries are stale from 08-20/08-21). The union gate predicts what mining WOULD ADMIT, not what verify() confirms at 0.90 precision, and not a score. The residual bucket is counted but not sub-classified (animation vs second object vs enemy) - next measurement, free.
